cards.text: Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet (Jeremiah 1:5), has a word from the LORD for the house of Israel. Just before this, the LORD said His people had gone after the Baals (Jeremiah 9:14). So grab a seat, friend, because today the LORD is talking about the gods people make for themselves.
The LORD starts here: do not learn the ways of the nations. Then He brings up the signs in the heavens, the ones the nations look up at and get TERRIFIED by.

cards.question: The nations are terrified by the signs in the heavens. The LORD tells Israel to be terrified of them too.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls the customs of the peoples worthless. And He walks through how one of their gods gets made, step by step, like a recipe card.

cards.question: Step one in making one of these gods. Where does it start out?

answers.text: A tree cut down from the forest
A stone dug up from the riverbed
A lump of clay from the potter

cards.text: A craftsman shapes it with a chisel, and then they cover it in silver and gold. Friend, that is a VERY expensive piece of firewood.

cards.question: Next, they fasten the silver and gold idol with hammer and nails. Why?

answers.text: So it faces the right way

cards.text: If your god needs NAILS to keep from tipping over, friend, you didn't get a god, you got furniture. Then the LORD gives a picture: their idols are like scarecrows in a cucumber patch.

cards.question: Like scarecrows, these idols cannot speak. And since they cannot walk, they must be ___.
The LORD tells Israel not to fear these idols. Why not?

answers.text: They can do no harm and no good
They are too far away to hurt anyone
The LORD has already broken them

cards.text: Then the prophet turns and talks right to the LORD: "There is none like You, O LORD." He says the LORD is great, and His name is mighty in power.

cards.question: The prophet calls the LORD the King of nations. He says that among all the wise men of the nations, a few come close to the LORD.

cards.text: Then he says the nations are senseless and foolish, taught by worthless idols made of wood. Friend, the mystery key I shared that junk drawer with never once figured out which door it opened, and even IT never tried to give anybody life advice.

cards.question: These idols get hammered silver from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz. Their blue and purple clothes are made by skilled workers.

cards.text: After all that silver, gold and fancy clothes, the prophet flips the whole thing with one little word: But. Friend, when the Bible says but, you LEAN in.

cards.question: But the LORD is the ___ God; He is the ___ God and eternal King.

cards.text: And this King is not sitting on a shelf waiting to be dusted. The earth quakes at His wrath, and the nations cannot endure His indignation.

cards.question: The LORD gives His people words to say about these idol gods. What do the words say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will perish from this earth
They will be locked away in a temple
They will be melted down into coins

cards.text: And the words point out that these gods made neither the heavens nor the earth. Friend, they couldn't make it across the ROOM without somebody carrying them.

cards.question: The prophet says the LORD made the earth by His power, established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding.
Then the prophet points to the sky in a storm. When the LORD thunders, what roars?

cards.text: He makes the clouds rise, sends lightning with the rain and brings the wind out of His storehouses. Meanwhile, every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols.

cards.question: The goldsmith's molten images are a fraud, and there is no ___ in them.

cards.text: The LORD runs thunder, lightning and wind, and these things can't even fog up a mirror. The prophet calls them worthless, a work to be mocked, and says they will perish in the time of their punishment.

cards.question: Last, the prophet calls the LORD the Portion of Jacob. Jacob is the father of Israel's twelve tribes (Genesis 49:28). Why is the Portion of Jacob not like these idols?

answers.text: He is the Maker of all things
He was shaped by the finest craftsman
He is covered in the purest gold

cards.question: The prophet says Israel is the tribe of the LORD's inheritance.

cards.text: The prophet closes with this: the LORD of Hosts is His name. Those idols needed a craftsman, a goldsmith and a box of nails just to stand up straight, but the LORD made the craftsman, the gold AND the whole forest.

findings.problem: The card says they 'cover it in silver and gold.' Jeremiah 10:4 says 'They adorn it with silver and gold.' Adorning is not the same as covering it entirely, so the card changes what the text calls the action.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says 'the nations are senseless and foolish.' Jeremiah 10:8 only says 'But they are altogether senseless and foolish,' and the nearest group before it is 'all the wise men of the nations' (10:7). The text doesn't say the nations as a whole, so naming them settles something the verse leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This true or false card restates Jeremiah 10:9 (silver from Tarshish, gold from Uphaz, blue and purple clothes) with no story card setting up that moment. The card before it covers 10:8. The baker can't reason it out and is left guessing True, so it reads like a test statement rather than a question that comes out of the story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: In the two-blank card, 'true' and 'living' both fit either blank equally well in meaning. Getting the order right ('true' first, 'living' second) depends on knowing the exact wording of Jeremiah 10:10, not on reasoning. A baker who swaps them could fairly argue they're right.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question says 'The LORD gives His people words to say.' Jeremiah 10:11 only says 'Thus you are to tell them' and doesn't say who gives the instruction. The walkthrough has just treated verses 6 to 10 as the prophet speaking to the LORD, so naming the LORD as the speaker settles something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Meanwhile, every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols' says the two things happen at the same time. Jeremiah 10:13-14 gives no time link between the LORD's storm and the goldsmith's shame.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card states 'The LORD runs thunder, lightning and wind,' which comes from Jeremiah 10:13. The card only cites Jeremiah 10:15, so its citation is narrower than the verses it tells. It should cite Jeremiah 10:13-15.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
